key_insight: PPy-PVA hydrogel geometry tunes drug transport through differences in microstructure and local electric fields, offering an alternative to current-density modulation.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-based hydrogel design could enable tunable iontophoretic delivery devices without individually adjusting current density.
method: Fabricated five BSA-loaded hydrogel geometries, including Hilbert curve-based designs.
Evaluated electric fields with finite element analysis and microstructure with scanning electron microscopy.
Measured passive and iontophoretic transport using Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes.
evidence_signal: The geometries produced distinct release, flux, and permeability profiles; average iontophoretic permeability was (3.80 ± 1.93) × 10^-5, with units unspecified in the abstract.
watch_item: Artificial-membrane results require validation in biological skin; the abstract reports finite element analysis, not an AI surrogate model.
paper_title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
